headline: On last trading day, Sensex crashed 1,000 points as FII selling wiped out ₹9.5 lakh crore

marketStatus.message: Market is closed for trading today due to an NSE holiday. It will reopen on Monday, 5 October.

why: En-masse selling by foreign investors (FIIs) across Indian equities
Surging global bond yields rattling markets and offsetting AI-stock optimism
Global rate hikes and oil price concerns sparking significant capital outflows
Technical weakness as the Sensex hit a fresh 52-week low during a four-session losing streak
whatHappening: Indian benchmark shares recorded their longest weekly losing run in 25 years
Investor wealth worth approximately ₹9.5 lakh crore was wiped out in a single day
TVS Motor and Coal India reported strong growth in September sales and production figures
Domestic passenger vehicle wholesales increased by 21% in September due to a low base
summary: On the last trading session, Indian markets suffered a massive sell-off with the Sensex plunging 1,000 points amid heavy foreign investor outflows. The decline marked the longest weekly losing streak in 25 years, wiping out over ₹9 lakh crore in investor wealth. Despite the broader market carnage, companies like TVS Motor and Coal India reported robust operational performance for September.
